--- title: "[Graph.personalized_pagerank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate Personalized PageRank with a custom restart distribution. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L33213-L33371){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.personalized_pagerank( personalization, damping=0.85, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Personalized PageRank](/assets/graphs/personalized-pagerank.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with the seed A (node id 1) outlined, every node shaded by PageRank whose random surfer always restarts at A. Rank stays near the seed, A 0.26, C 0.23 and B 0.20, and fades along the strip to F 0.05 and G 0.02." width="100%"} Unlike standard PageRank where the random surfer teleports uniformly to any node, Personalized PageRank teleports back to seed nodes with probabilities given by `personalization`. This makes it the primary method for gene prioritization in genome-wide association studies (GWAS): seed nodes are GWAS hits, and the resulting scores rank candidate genes by network proximity to those hits. The scores are computed by power iteration. At each step a surfer follows a random outgoing edge with probability `damping=` and otherwise jumps back to a seed, picked in proportion to its personalization value. A node with no outgoing edges sends all of its rank back to the seeds. The resulting score of a node is the long-run fraction of time the surfer spends there, so nodes that are close to the seeds and reachable along many paths score highest. Typical uses besides gene prioritization: - "related items" ranking: which nodes matter most from the point of view of one node or a small set of nodes - local community detection around a seed set - comparing the influence of different seed sets on the same network In directed graphs the surfer only moves along edge direction; in undirected graphs it can move either way. Edge weights are not used: every outgoing edge is equally likely. `random_walk_with_restart()` computes the same scores with `restart_prob = 1 - damping`. The scores are written to the node DataFrame every time, including when `return_dict=True`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [personalization]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping node IDs to restart probabilities. Values are normalized internally, so they don't need to sum to 1. Nodes not in the dictionary have zero restart probability. Use a single entry for one seed, or several entries with larger values for seeds you trust more. IDs that are not in the graph are ignored. [damping]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.85]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Probability of following an edge (vs. teleporting back to a seed). Higher values let the walk spread further from the seeds. Typical range: `0.5`-`0.95`. The default is `0.85`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of power-iteration steps. The default is `100`, which is enough for the default `damping=` on most graphs; values of `damping=` close to `1` converge more slowly and may need more. If the limit is reached, the current scores are returned without warning. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance. Iteration stops once the summed absolute change in all scores (the L1 norm of the change) between two steps falls below this value. The default is `1e-6`; smaller values give more precise scores at the cost of more iterations. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name for storing scores in the node DataFrame. Defaults to `"personalized_pagerank"`. An existing column with this name is overwritten. Use different names to keep results from several seed sets side by side. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns the score dictionary without writing anything to the graph. If `False` (default), stores scores in the node DataFrame and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to scores (sum to `1.0`). Otherwise returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `personalization=` is empty or its values do not sum to a positive number. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Starting every restart from `GeneA` keeps most of the rank there. `GeneD` comes second because it is reached both directly from `GeneA` and at the end of the longer path, and as a dead end it sends its rank straight back to `GeneA`: ::: {#e695752f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["GeneA", "GeneB", "GeneC", "GeneD"]) .add_edges( [("GeneA", "GeneB"), ("GeneB", "GeneC"), ("GeneC", "GeneD"), ("GeneA", "GeneD")] ) ) seed_id = graph.get_id_from_label("GeneA") scores = graph.personalized_pagerank( personalization={seed_id: 1.0}, return_dict=True, ) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 4) for nid, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'GeneC': 0.1434, 'GeneA': 0.3971, 'GeneD': 0.2907, 'GeneB': 0.1688} ``` ::: ::: Lowering `damping=` makes the surfer restart more often, so the rank stays even closer to the seed: `GeneA` gains, and `GeneC`, two steps away, loses about half of its score: ::: {#361645c8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} scores = graph.personalized_pagerank( personalization={seed_id: 1.0}, damping=0.5, return_dict=True, ) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 4) for nid, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'GeneC': 0.0741, 'GeneA': 0.5926, 'GeneD': 0.1852, 'GeneB': 0.1481} ``` ::: ::: Several seeds can be weighted differently. In two triangles joined by a short path, giving `G` three times the restart weight of `A` pulls most of the rank toward the `E`, `F`, `G` triangle. With `return_dict=False`, the scores land in the node DataFrame: ::: {#393424a6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph() g.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"]) g.add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("E", "G"), ("F", "G"), ] ) seeds = {g.get_id_from_label("A"): 1.0, g.get_id_from_label("G"): 3.0} g.personalized_pagerank(seeds, attr_name="ppr") g.get_node_df().select(["label", "ppr"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
